hero.lead: The world’s largest oil exporter, a nation of 37 million financing Vision 2030, which raised $11.5 billion in international bonds in January 2026 under a $58 billion borrowing plan.

capital.heading: The busiest sovereign borrower in the emerging world.

record.text: Four-tranche international bonds under the Global Medium-Term Note Programme, January 2026; orders about $31 billion
2026 borrowing plan, approved January 2026: about SAR 165 billion for the deficit and SAR 52 billion of principal; declared complete in May 2026
Seven-year syndicated loan for power, water and public utilities projects, arranged December 2025
First sovereign green bond, seven years, priced February 2025; its net proceeds allocated by March 2026
Public debt, share of GDP, 2025; the IMF projects 32.1% for 2026 (Article IV, July 2026)

register.name: International sukuk, five and ten years
register.detail: National Debt Management Center · KSA Ijara Sukuk Limited, Ijarah structure · $1.25bn due 2031 and $2bn due 2036 · September 2026
register.note: Orders of about $16.5 billion, about five times the issue; the Kingdom’s second international sukuk on an Ijarah structure
register.text: International trust certificates (sukuk) of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, issued under the Global Trust Certificate Issuance Program to meet the Kingdom’s financing needs in international debt markets. They fund the budget as a whole; the announcement names no one of the seven standards.

register.name: International sukuk for housing finance, Saudi Real Estate Refinance Company
register.detail: Saudi Real Estate Refinance Company, a PIF company · guaranteed by the Government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia · $1.25bn over 5.5 years and $1.5bn over 10 years · priced 9 July 2026
register.note: 6.8 times oversubscribed, mainly by international investors; the International Sukuk Programme raised from $5 billion to $10 billion
register.text: Sukuk of the Saudi Real Estate Refinance Company, established by the Public Investment Fund in 2017, which provides liquidity to financiers so that they can offer housing finance to individuals. It serves the shelter standard: its Chairman links the issue to the Housing Program of Vision 2030 and to enabling Saudi families to own homes.

register.name: International bonds, four tranches
register.detail: National Debt Management Center · Global Medium-Term Note Programme · $2.5bn of 3 years, $2.75bn of 5 years, $2.75bn of 10 years and $3.5bn of 30 years · January 2026
register.note: Orders of about $31 billion, 2.7 times the issue
register.text: The Kingdom’s first international bond issue of 2026, made under the Annual Borrowing Plan to widen the investor base and meet financing needs in international debt markets. The bonds fund the budget as a whole; the announcement names no one of the seven standards.

register.name: Syndicated loan for power, water and public utilities
register.detail: National Debt Management Center · seven years · arranged 31 December 2025
register.note: Under the Kingdom’s Medium-Term Debt Strategy; the lending banks are not named
register.text: A seven-year syndicated loan arranged by the National Debt Management Center to support power, water and public utilities projects. It serves the water and energy standards through the utilities it finances.

register.name: Seven- and twelve-year euro bonds, with the first sovereign green tranche
register.detail: National Debt Management Center · green tranche of €1.5bn, 7 years, coupon 3.375%, due 5 March 2032 · €750M of 12 years, due 2037 · priced 25 February 2025
register.note: Orders of about €10 billion, about four times the issue; the green proceeds allocated by March 2026
register.text: The first issue of the Government of Saudi Arabia to include a green tranche, part of an initiative under the Financial Sector Development Program to support the Kingdom’s sustainability goals and net-zero emissions. The allocation report of March 2026 places 75.2% of the green proceeds in the sustainable management of living natural resources and land use, 9.4% in climate change adaptation, 6.2% in renewable energy, 5% in energy efficiency and 4.3% in biodiversity, and reports no allocation to water and wastewater.

register.name: Financing for water and energy procurement, NEXI
register.detail: National Debt Management Center and Nippon Export and Investment Insurance (NEXI) · twelve years · announced 15 January 2026 at the Saudi–Japanese Roundtable in Riyadh
register.note: The 2026 borrowing plan names export credit agencies among the sources of alternative government funding
register.text: A twelve-year financing agreement arranged by the National Debt Management Center with the Japanese export credit agency to support procurement in the water and energy sectors. It serves the water and energy standards; the announcement names no lending banks and gives no other terms.
